edges.effect_quant: The best recent cohort synthesis estimated about a 12% lower renal-cancer risk in higher coffee consumers, but older pooled evidence was closer to null.
edges.mechanism: Coffee delivers chlorogenic acids and other compounds that may improve insulin sensitivity and reduce oxidative injury in renal tissue. Any real benefit is likely modest, because the observational signal is inconsistent and may vary by coffee type, smoking, and adiposity.
edges.summary: The most current cohort-only meta-analysis leans toward a small protective association, but the overall literature is not settled. Older pooled analyses of renal or urologic cancers were essentially null, so the fairest summary is suggestive benefit with enough inconsistency to keep confidence moderate at best.
edges.caveats: Some studies focus specifically on renal cell carcinoma, while others pool broader renal or urologic outcomes. Residual confounding by smoking, BMI, and correlated diet patterns could easily account for part of the apparent protection.
